active_dockets.title: Regulating Mini-Excavators (15–35 HP) on Hill Slopes, and Protecting Traditional Contour Terraces
active_dockets.status: ACTIVE • RTI APPLICATIONS SENT BY RPAD (26.10.2026)
active_dockets.latest_update: RTI applications sent to the Collectorate & Joint Director of Horticulture; field documentation of slope alterations at Kookal–Kurumudi Road recorded for administrative follow-up.
statutory_enactments: Disaster Management Act, 2005 (Sections 30, 34, 51)
District Collector Standing Order / Regulation Directive dated 02.03.2021 (Strict curbs on mechanical earthmovers on slopes)
Tamil Nadu District Municipalities (Hill Stations) Building Rules, 1993
Hill Area Conservation Authority (HACA) Mandatory Regulations
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 (Sections 3 & 5)
official_respondents: The District Collector & Chairperson, District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA), The Nilgiris
The Executive Engineer, Agricultural Engineering Department, Udhagamandalam
The Regional Transport Officer (RTO), The Nilgiris Division
The Tahsildars of Kotagiri, Coonoor, and Udhagamandalam Taluks
active_dockets.incident_trigger: Heavy rain of 200–250 mm across the Kotagiri and Coonoor ridges on 22–24 October 2026 led to landslides, slope failures and mudflows. Many of these areas had recently been altered by small excavators (15–35 HP) cutting steep vertical faces into fragile tea and agricultural terraces without the required permissions.
relief_sought: GPS registration and verifiable operating permits for all 15–35 HP tracked mini-excavators working in the Nilgiris.
Consistent field enforcement of the District Collector's directive of 02.03.2021, requiring geotechnical and Agricultural Engineering vetting before steep slopes are cut.
Prompt stop-work and restoration measures, including retaining walls, at identified sites.
active_dockets.dossier_summary: Drone mapping, machine deployment records and RTI requests on machine licensing are being compiled.

active_dockets.title: Closed-Loop Effluent Treatment & Silt-Traps for Commercial Vegetable-Washing Units under the Water Act, 1974
statutory_enactments: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 (Sections 24, 25, 33A)
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 (Sections 7, 8)
Tamil Nadu River Basin Protection Guidelines
The Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017
official_respondents: The District Environmental Engineer, Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board (TNPCB), Udhagamandalam
The Member Secretary, Tamil Nadu State Wetland Authority, Chennai
The Joint Director of Agriculture, Nilgiris District
The Executive Officers / Commissioners of Concerned Town Panchayats (Kotagiri, Ketti Valley)
active_dockets.incident_trigger: Sustained unmonitored operation of industrial-scale carrot and root-vegetable washing stations situated along natural perennial stream courses. These facilities abstract massive volumes of riparian surface water and release untreated, turbid wastewater dense with eroded volcanic silt, synthetic pesticides, fungicides, and chemical fertilizers directly into tributaries of the Bhavani and Moyar basins.
relief_sought: Mandate installation of standardized three-chamber sedimentation tanks and closed-loop water recirculation systems for all commercial vegetable-washing establishments.
Immediate prohibition of raw slurry discharge and silt dumping into perennial streams, natural marshlands, and drainage gullies.
Institution of regular quarterly physicochemical and ecotoxicological water quality audits by TNPCB at all major washing cluster outflows.
active_dockets.dossier_summary: 14 active commercial washing locations documented with water sampling reports, turbidity measurements exceeding permissible standards by over 400%, and photographic proof of downstream siltation choking natural shola wetland beds.

active_dockets.incident_trigger: Failure of administrative authorities to act upon 24+ verified civic representations submitted between 2021 and 2026. These detailed ongoing illegal commercial developments, luxury guest houses, and earth-filling inside designated Reserve Forest 100-meter buffer strips, social forestry plantations, and seasonal wetland riparian corridors.
relief_sought: Independent joint GIS boundary demarcation of forest fringes and waterways by Revenue and Forest survey wings.
Resolution of provisional building clearances granted contrary to mandatory HACA and Eco-Sensitive Buffer restrictions.
Administrative representations requesting time-bound review and restoration.
active_dockets.dossier_summary: Consolidated paper trail comprising certified copies of unanswered petitions, survey department cadastre maps, satellite chronological time-lapse imagery demonstrating buffer encroachment, and municipal sanction irregularities.

active_dockets.incident_trigger: Systematic earth-filling, leveling, and permanent destruction of high-altitude valley sponge wetlands, perennial peat marshes, and shola swamps in Kotagiri, Ooty, and Kundah basins, combined with heavy commercial extraction from unmetered borewells drying up downstream natural springs and municipal drinking water intakes.
relief_sought: GPS cadastral demarcation of montane wetland sponges and peat bogs across the Nilgiris.
Permanent restriction on soil-filling, ditching, and construction within designated wetland marsh buffers.
Digital flow-metering and extraction limits on commercial borewells.
active_dockets.dossier_summary: Hydrological audit dossier compiling spring discharge rates, borewell GPS mapping, and historical satellite time-lapse data documenting the loss of critical watershed sponge wetlands.

active_dockets.title: A Quieter Season for Migratory Birds and Wildlife: High-Decibel Restriction in the Nilgiris
active_dockets.latest_update: A statutory notice and RTI application were sent by RPAD on 26.10.2026 to the District Collector, Field Director (MTR), DFOs, TNPCB and SP Nilgiris, requesting prohibitory orders under Sec 163 BNSS and enforcement of noise-pollution norms in the festival season.

active_dockets.incident_trigger: Over 60% of the Nilgiris district is forest, and almost every settlement, including many holiday villas and resorts, lies on a forest fringe or wildlife corridor. Each year from October to November, during peak winter bird migration, high-decibel pyrotechnics cause acute distress to wildlife and disrupt nesting birds.
relief_sought: Prohibitory orders under Section 163 BNSS restricting high-decibel firecrackers in ecologically sensitive forest fringe settlements and avian flyways.
Strict enforcement of the Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000 across the district during festival periods.
Public awareness campaigns encouraging quiet, eco-friendly celebrations.
active_dockets.dossier_summary: Statutory notice and RTI application sent by RPAD on 26.10.2026 to the District Collector and Superintendent of Police in continuation of representations submitted since October 2023.

past_interventions.title: Halting the 6,000 Sq. Ft. Concrete Construction Inside Longwood Shola Reserve Forest (Kotagiri)
past_interventions.summary: Spearheaded sustained public agitation, environmental fact-finding, and official representations against the Tamil Nadu Forest Department's proposal to construct a massive 6,000 sq. ft. concrete interpretation center inside the pristine, ancient Longwood Shola Reserve Forest—the sole surviving high-altitude urban shola and pivotal micro-watershed supplying drinking water to Kotagiri town. Following overwhelming public outcry, ecological evidence presentation, and sustained media coverage, the state government formally abandoned the interior forest construction plan.

press_citation.title: Protests against construction in Longwood Shola Reserve Forest intensify in the Nilgiris

key_outcomes: Complete withdrawal of the 6,000 sq. ft. concrete construction proposal inside the Reserve Forest boundary.
Preservation of undisturbed canopy and vital groundwater aquifer feeding Kotagiri.
Establishment of institutional vigilance and community stewardship over the Ramsar-recognized ecosystem.
past_interventions.locus_standi_relevance: Direct proof of organizational capacity to mobilize community oversight, substantiate scientific grievances, and enforce preservation of ecologically vulnerable public commons.

past_interventions.title: Wildlife Crime Surveillance & Anti-Poaching Apprehension
past_interventions.summary: Conducted covert ground tracking and intelligence gathering on illegal wire snares, small-mammal poaching, and bird trapping across the plantation-forest interface. Documented active wildlife poaching and handed over definitive geolocated evidence directly to the Tamil Nadu Forest Department flying squad, resulting in an immediate raid, apprehension of the accused, and formal registration of a wildlife offense case under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.
key_outcomes: Immediate apprehension of poacher and confiscation of crude snares and illicit implements.
Formal registration of statutory Wildlife Offense Case by Tamil Nadu Forest Department.
Routine de-snaring patrols instituted along critical corridor borders.
past_interventions.locus_standi_relevance: Established credible evidentiary field surveillance capability and proactive cooperation with statutory forest enforcement agencies.

past_interventions.title: Reserve Forest Buffer Zone Surveillance & Illegal Tree-Felling Injunctions
past_interventions.category: Buffer Zone Vigilance & Forest Act Representations
past_interventions.summary: Systematically surveyed and exposed illegal commercial resort developments attempting to bypass the 100-meter statutory Reserve Forest buffer perimeter. Formally lodged detailed representations with the District Collector and DFO detailing unpermitted nighttime felling of native shola trees and slope-stabilizing canopy on private holdings, triggering official spot inspections and penalty proceedings.
key_outcomes: Official spot-inspections conducted by Forest Rangers on reported illegal tree-felling coordinates.
Halt on unauthorized grading operations adjacent to Reserve Forest boundaries.
Comprehensive photo-archive of forest fringe incursions created for ongoing legal dockets.
past_interventions.locus_standi_relevance: Direct administrative engagement highlighting systemic enforcement bottlenecks that necessitate structured judicial remedies.

past_interventions.title: Social Forestry & Poramboke Riverbank Encroachment Petitions
past_interventions.summary: Carried out continuous administrative petitioning against the illicit conversion of government social forestry reserves, grazing poramboke, and stream headwaters into commercial tea estates and private residential layouts. Leveraged historical revenue village maps to pinpoint unrecorded encroachments on drainage pathways.
key_outcomes: Administrative notices issued by Revenue Tahsildar to clear obstructed feeder streams.
Prevented physical diversion of two perennial natural spring corridors.
Built comprehensive evidentiary register of unaddressed representations for the 2026 Special Forest Bench filings.
past_interventions.locus_standi_relevance: Forms the foundational evidentiary basis of Docket THF/LEGAL/NIL-BF/2026/003.

past_interventions.title: Grassroots Ecological Restoration with 'Forest First'
past_interventions.summary: In parallel with regulatory vigilance, fostered the hands-on ecological restoration of degraded shola-grassland patches and riparian wetlands in the Nilgiris through our restoration campaign Forest First (forestfirst.org). Eradicated invasive alien wattle and cestrum while propagating endemic shola saplings and native tussock grasses to stabilize eroded slopes.
key_outcomes: Successful revival of endemic micro-habitats and shola species nursery.
Demonstrated that ecological defense must walk hand-in-hand with restorative field science.
past_interventions.locus_standi_relevance: Grounds our legal advocacy in profound, practical domain expertise in montane forest hydrology and native flora.

crisis_matrix.name: Unregulated Tracked Mini-Excavators & Slope Terracing
crisis_matrix.primary_driver: Rapid proliferation of 15–35 HP compact tracked backhoes ('Mini Kubota') hired informally to slice vertical 70–90° cuts into high-gradient hillsides for unpermitted residential and agricultural plots.
crisis_matrix.ecological_consequence: Destruction of centuries-old Badaga contour terraces, structural fracturing of sub-surface colluvium, and severe landslide failure during high-intensity rainfall events (200mm+), as seen in the late October 2026 disasters.
crisis_matrix.statutory_anchor: Disaster Management Act 2005; Nilgiris District Collector Order 02.03.2021
crisis_matrix.action_pathway: Mandatory GPS fleet tracking, strict permit gatekeeping, and judicial injunctions against unpermitted machines.

crisis_matrix.name: Commercial Vegetable-Washing Effluent & Stream Siltation
crisis_matrix.primary_driver: Industrial-scale washing of root vegetables (carrots, potatoes) directly within or adjacent to perennial hill streams without silt retention or wastewater treatment.
crisis_matrix.ecological_consequence: Millions of litres of topsoil slurry laced with pesticide residues discharged into Moyar and Bhavani headwaters. Massive silt deposition suffocates riverbed gravel, extirpates endemic fish/amphibian breeding zones, and fills reservoirs.
crisis_matrix.statutory_anchor: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1974; Environment (Protection) Act 1986
crisis_matrix.action_pathway: Mandatory closed-loop effluent recycling, settling ponds, and pollution control compliance.

crisis_matrix.name: Reserve Forest Perimeter & Buffer Encroachment
crisis_matrix.primary_driver: Gradual expansion of resort estates, concrete retaining walls, and tourist cottages within the mandatory 100-metre buffer perimeter of declared Reserve Forests.
crisis_matrix.ecological_consequence: Interruption of wildlife migratory routes (Gaur, Leopard, Asian Elephant, Nilgiri Tahr), heightened human-wildlife conflict, and canopy fragmentation along sensitive forest fringes.
crisis_matrix.statutory_anchor: Tamil Nadu Forest Act 1882; Supreme Court Orders in Godavarman Batch; HACA Norms
crisis_matrix.action_pathway: Composite pre-litigation notice before Madras High Court Special Forest Bench and demolition of unauthorized buffer edifices.

crisis_matrix.name: Riparian Wetland & Poramboke Watershed Drainage
crisis_matrix.risk_level: Severe / Loss of Town Drinking Water
crisis_matrix.primary_driver: Dumping of construction debris and agricultural conversion in valley bottom wetlands (vavus/bogs) that act as natural sponge aquifers for hill settlements.
crisis_matrix.ecological_consequence: Flash flooding during monsoons followed by severe acute water scarcity in Kotagiri, Coonoor, and Ooty during summer months.
crisis_matrix.statutory_anchor: Wetlands Rules 2017; TN Protection of Tanks & Eviction of Encroachment Act 2007
crisis_matrix.action_pathway: Cadastral survey boundary protection, restoration of sponge hydrology with Forest First.
